messages.subject: Stat smooth
parts:
Following code plots 3 separate regression lines for each factor of 'cyl':

(mtcarsPlot <- ggplot(mtcars,aes(x=disp,y=mpg,colour=as.factor(cyl))) + 
  geom_point(size=8) +
  stat_smooth(method='lm')) 

How can I plot a single regression line (no subsetting for 'cyl')?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Stat smooth
parts:
Hi:

Another way to do this is to remove the color aesthetic from the ggplot() call and move it to geom_point() instead:

ggplot(mtcars,aes(x=disp,y=mpg)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = as.factor(cyl))) +
    geom_smooth(method = lm)

Placing the color aesthetic in the ggplot() call means that it will be expected to be present in *all* subsequent layers, which forces one to use group = 1 as an aesthetic in geom_smooth() to override the expectation of separate lines by levels of the color aesthetic.

Both methods are instructive and worth understanding: e.g., if I had multiple layers in a ggplot, most of which used color (say, for example, colored boxplots and points) then I'd probably put the color aesthetic in ggplot() and use the group = 1 device for geom_smooth() as Ben showed. OTOH, if I only wanted color in one or two layers of a multi-layer ggplot, I would declare them as aesthetics in the geom(s) of interest and not in ggplot(), as in my code above.

Dennis
